passage: In Chhindwara the power had gone off again, but everyone's phones still glowed. Darshan was on the rooftop with his phone, scrolling the class group. Someone had posted a blurry photo of Madhav and Leela sharing an umbrella near the bus stand. Darshan typed, "Umbrella couple!" with a laughing face. Within a minute there were twenty replies. Someone added that they held hands. Someone else said her father had seen them at the fair. Darshan felt the rush of it and wrote, "Wedding in March," and more laughing faces piled up. Then Leela's cousin posted, "She was just walking home, stop it." But by then the screenshots were already in three other groups, and the correction sat unread at the bottom.

qa.q: What did Darshan type in the class group?
qa.a: He typed "Umbrella couple!" with a laughing face.

qa.q: What was Darshan feeling as the replies piled up?
qa.a: He felt a rush of fun and attention, enjoying how quickly everyone joined his joke.

qa.q: What turning point was available before Darshan wrote "Wedding in March"?
qa.a: He could have stopped adding to it, or even supported the cousin's correction, instead of feeding a story that was already spreading beyond the group.

qa.q: How might Leela be affected by the chat now?
qa.a: She may feel exposed and helpless, because the screenshots are in other groups and her cousin's correction was ignored.

grounding: It shows a guess posted in a group chat with laughing emojis, details added and screenshots spread faster than a correction.

passage: It was a grey afternoon in Gothenburg when Oskar posted in the year-nine chat: "Chen and Alva left the party early together 👀" with a laughing emoji. Mia replied with three laughing faces. Someone added that Alva had been crying. Someone else said Chen's jacket was in her locker. None of it had been checked. Oskar watched the numbers climb on his phone and added a joke about a wedding cake. It felt like a game. By evening, Chen messaged the group himself: "I walked her to the tram because she felt sick. That's it." Four people reacted with a thumbs up. But forty had already seen the screenshots, and they were sitting in other chats that Chen would never be able to reach.

qa.q: Why did Chen say he walked Alva to the tram?
qa.a: He said he walked her to the tram because she felt sick.

qa.q: Why did Oskar keep adding jokes as the numbers climbed?
qa.a: He enjoyed the attention and amusement; to him it felt like a game rather than something that could hurt.

qa.q: What could Oskar do now to reduce the harm?
qa.a: He could delete his posts, say publicly that Chen's explanation is true, and ask others to stop forwarding the screenshots, even though he cannot pull them all back.

qa.q: What is it like for Chen and Alva after the chat blows up?
qa.a: They are likely embarrassed and frustrated, because Chen's honest correction reaches only a few people while the story keeps moving.

grounding: It illustrates a guess spreading in a group chat with laughing emojis and added details, moving faster than the correction can follow.

passage:
It was the night before the chemistry exam, and the power had gone out in half of Lucknow, so everyone was on their phones by candlelight instead of studying.

Mehak was bored. In the class group chat she typed: "Tushar and Isha were in the library for TWO hours today 😆 study date??"

Within a minute, someone replied with three laughing faces. Someone else posted a photo of Tushar and Isha at the library table, taken from across the room. Then someone wrote, "I heard they hold hands under the table."

Mehak hadn't heard that. Nobody had. But now it was there.

She saw someone had screenshotted the whole thing and posted it in the other section's group.

Tushar typed: "We were doing the practical file. Stop." But his message was buried under forty new ones, and Mehak's joke kept travelling, faster than she could have called it back.

qa.q: What was Tushar and Isha actually doing in the library, according to Tushar?
qa.a: Doing the practical file.

qa.q: How might Mehak feel when she sees the screenshot in the other section's group?
qa.a: She probably feels uneasy and a little alarmed, realising her joke has spread beyond her control.

qa.q: What could Mehak do now, even though the story can't be fully called back?
qa.a: Delete her message, post that it was only a joke and not true, and apologise to Tushar and Isha directly.

qa.q: What is it like for Tushar when his correction gets buried?
qa.a: He feels frustrated and helpless, watching the rumour move faster than his explanation.

grounding: During a power cut before an exam, Mehak's joking guess in a group chat is screenshotted and embellished, moving faster than any correction.

passage:
Devika posted it without thinking, on the auto ride home from school in Pune: "Guess who shared an umbrella today 👀😆" with a blurry photo of Karan and Nidhi at the gate.

By the time she reached home, the class group had exploded. Jaya had screenshotted it and sent it to the dance class group. Someone had added, "They were holding hands too." Someone else drew a heart around them in the photo.

Devika hadn't seen any hand-holding. She wasn't even sure it was them in the photo.

At dinner she scrolled through, eating nothing. Nidhi had posted, "It was raining, we live next door, grow up." Only two people had seen it. The heart-drawing had seventy reactions.

Devika deleted her original post. But the screenshots were everywhere, and she couldn't delete those.

qa.q: Who screenshotted Devika's post and sent it to the dance class group?
qa.a: Jaya.

qa.q: How does Devika feel at dinner, scrolling without eating?
qa.a: She feels guilty and anxious, seeing her post spread and grow beyond what she ever saw.

qa.q: What could Devika still do?
qa.a: Apologise to Karan and Nidhi directly and post clearly that the story wasn't true, even though she can't delete the screenshots.

qa.q: How might Nidhi feel seeing her explanation get two views while the heart gets seventy reactions?
qa.a: She probably feels frustrated and powerless, as the rumour outruns her correction.

grounding: Devika's joking post about two classmates is screenshotted and embellished across groups, showing how online stories outrun any correction.

passage:
"Keerthana, did you see what I posted in the group?"

"The one about Aman and Riddhi? Yusuf, why did you post that?"

"It was a joke. I just said they looked cosy at the canteen."

"With a laughing emoji. And now someone's added that they were kissing behind the lab."

"What? I never said that!"

"Doesn't matter. Look, someone's made a sticker of them."

"Okay, I'll delete it."

"Deleting yours won't help. It's been screenshotted into three other groups."

"Three?"

"Four now. Your cousin's school too."

"I didn't mean for this to happen."

"I know. But it's out now. You can't pull it back."

"What do I do?"

"Start by telling Aman and Riddhi you're sorry. Then tell the group clearly it's not true. And maybe tell Ma'am before it gets worse."

qa.q: How many groups had the post been screenshotted into by the end?
qa.a: Four.

qa.q: How does Yusuf feel when he hears about the kissing detail?
qa.a: Yusuf feels shocked and alarmed, having never said that, and guilty that the joke grew so fast.

qa.q: What does Keerthana advise, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: Apologise to Aman and Riddhi, correct the story clearly, and tell Ma'am, because deleting alone can't pull back the screenshots.

qa.q: What might Aman and Riddhi be going through as the sticker spreads?
qa.a: They are probably embarrassed and upset, with a false story about them moving faster than any correction.

grounding: In dialogue Yusuf's joking post with a laughing emoji is screenshotted and embellished across groups, showing online rumours can't be called back.

passage: It was one line. That's what I keep telling myself. Last October I typed in our class group, "Amandeep and Rhea came out of the library together AGAIN, wedding when?" and added a laughing emoji. I thought it was funny for about four seconds. Within ten minutes someone had screenshotted it into another group. By evening someone else had added that they had been seen holding hands at the bus stop, which I never said and which, as far as I know, never happened. By morning there was a photo of them edited with hearts. I deleted my message at 11 p.m., panicking. It didn't matter. The screenshots were already everywhere, like seeds in the wind. Amandeep didn't come to class that Friday. On Monday our class teacher called me in and said, "Asif, tell me what happened." I told her everything. I still think about how fast my one line stopped being mine.

qa.q: What did Asif add to the line in the class group?
qa.a: Asif added a laughing emoji.

qa.q: What was Asif feeling when deleting the message at 11 p.m.?
qa.a: Asif was panicking and guilty, realising the joke had grown into something false and hurtful that could not be taken back.

qa.q: What could Asif have done the moment the first screenshot appeared?
qa.a: Asif could have posted a clear correction, asked people not to forward it, and told a teacher straight away, rather than only deleting the line late at night.

qa.q: What might Amandeep have been going through that Friday?
qa.a: Amandeep was probably embarrassed and hurt by the edited photo and invented details, perhaps staying home to avoid the stares.

grounding: Shows a guess posted in a group chat with a laughing emoji being screenshotted and embellished faster than any correction could follow.
